newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares index down, but UES perks up.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares index down, but UES perks up.

text.p: The Russian Trading System index fell 1.26 percent on Friday but some traders said an end to a recent price slide could be in sight as some leading shares had picked up in afternoon trading.
The RTS 23-share index fell to 309.41 on a very low volume of $23.1 million for the entire market.
But power utility UES regained the 20 cent level, which it fell past in morning trade, to close at $0.2120 after $0.2040 on Thursday. Truck maker Kamaz rose to $1.59 from $1.47.

Dmitry Voronkov, chief trader at MFK-Moscow Partners, said some shares firmed on support by domestic operators encouraged by strong openings on European bourses and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's statement natural monopolies would not be cut up.
"The general market will not die, and the general uptrend will not change," he said.
UFG trader Maxim Perlin said the market, which fears a hike in U.S. interest rates, could move either way next week when a Federal Reserve policy-making committee will discuss the issue.

"I'd bet on the Federal Reserve System," he said. "That is the deciding factor for Western investors now. Isn't it strange how the Russian market is showing more and more correlation with the Western ones?"
